entities.summary: Guillaume Gouffier, seigneur de Bonnivet, was a French soldier and diplomat who played a crucial role in the Italian Wars. Born in the late 15th century, Gouffier served under various French commanders, including Francis I, and was instrumental in several key battles. He was appointed as the ambassador to the Holy Roman Empire in 1517, where he negotiated the Treaty of London, securing a vital alliance for France. Gouffier's military prowess and diplomatic skills made him a trusted advisor to Francis I, and he was later appointed as the president of the French army in Italy. He died on February 24, 1525, in the midst of the Italian Wars, leaving behind a legacy as one of France's most accomplished soldiers of his time. His legacy can be seen in the modern French military, which continues to honor his memory with the 'Ordre du Gouffier de Bonnivet,' a prestigious order of merit established in his honor.
